problems.memo_sentence: The authors propose customized gate-based quantum algorithms that evaluate exp(−αx′) and Gaussian functions via sequences of controlled multiplications by precomputed constants Ai, with Gaussian evaluation adding an extra multiplication to compute x^2. The basic algorithm uses d controlled multiplications with space scaling as dn + n + d qubits, and they refine it by reusing a single Ai register via NOT-pattern transformations, skipping negligible multipliers so that the number of multiplications m scales as log n, and adding a second-half OR/SWAP circuit to handle truncation when m < d.
problems.source_evidence: “For the Gaussian function, i.e. f(x′) = exp(−αx′2), one proceeds in exactly the same manner, except that it is necessary to perform an additional multiplication, to obtain x2 from x. We note that there are some specialized quantum squaring algorithms, that shave a bit off of the cost of a generic multiplication… If d ≪ n however, this savings is not significant; the cost of the extra multiplication itself is much less than the others, since it involves only d rather than n qubits.”
problems.explanation: The memo states the Gaussian case simply adds one multiplication, but the paper adds an important caveat: specialized squaring algorithms can reduce that cost slightly, even if the savings are usually not significant in the d ≪ n regime.
